lines.text: Every month, a founder proves their own numbers at eleven o'clock. No controller. No finance team. This is the close when nobody is left to do it.

The close is six steps. Pull the data. Match the invoices. Work the unmatched list. Post the journals. Tie out the balances. Get it approved. The first two are solved — Seapoint does them. The third is a person at eleven o'clock, choosing account codes from memory.
So we handed it the books. Seapoint MCP, read with my own permissions. One question: a hundred and sixty-two thousand pounds of September spend, twelve categories.

Then nobody asks. Of two thousand six hundred and sixty-four transactions, two thousand six hundred and twenty-nine clear themselves. Fourteen need a human. Point five per cent. And what that human gets isn't a wall of output — fourteen lines, each with a reason.

Then it has to earn the answer. Activate a rule before validating it: refused. One happy case: still refused. Seven labeled replays, zero regressions — only then. And nothing gets written until I say so.

And this is the one I'd show a partner. Meridian Insurance, twelve hundred and forty. Filed as legal fees, coded as insurance, no receipt. Two hundred and forty-eight pounds of VAT rides on which one is right. It won't write it. It shows me the contradiction instead.

Everyone in AI accounting sells you accuracy. Ninety-seven point eight per cent, taken on faith. We sell the point five per cent it won't take on faith. Enterprise software needs a controller and a hundred and fifty thousand a year. A twelve-person startup has neither. close-keeper.
